segments.text: AHHHHH!

The doxorubicin will scar the muscles slow and deep 250 marks the modern line, no dose you give is cheap The first year is when most will show, not decades down the line The echo tells you when it starts, the F in decline Trastuzumab attacks the same, the F starts to fall The parent takes the heart, not long, the payload takes them all But stop the drug and give it time, the F will come back So echo first, then echo through and keep the heart on track
And the 5-FU will clamp the flow, a spasm, not a clot.
Capacitabine does the same, the chest pain comes on hot.
It hits them while the drug still runs, not days or weeks away.
The troponin may still be clear, so hold the drug today.
Carfilzomib will fail the heart and cycle on the worst.
The myeloma patient swells, the BNP comes first.
It looks like simple overload, but that is not the source.
So order up an echo now and hold the drugs next course.
Thank you.

Imprunitinib will bring the fib and bleeding side by side The rhythm breaks, the pressure climbs, a difficult divide You want to thin the blood for stroke but bleeding is the cost So check the rhythm every time or else the beat is lost The arsenic will stretch QT and nilotinib too Osimertinib does the same, ondansetron runs through Together they can stack the risks, so fix the lights today So check the EKG each time or torsades leads the way Sunitinib and sorafenib, lenbatinib as well
Babasazumab does the same and blood pressure will swell.
It marks the drug is working right, so treat it, do not stop.
But watch for clots and failing heart when pressure hits the top.
Potatinib will clot the line, the arteries, not veins.
A stroke can have my limb that dies, that's what the box explains.
Nilotinib and tacitinib can do the vessel harm.
So check.
The pulses check the legs and sound the right alarm.
The checkpoints hit the heart as well.
It's rare, it comes on fast.
The first two doses, weeks, not months, and one in three won't last.
The epinephrine lifts the risk near five times over one.
The EF can be normal still.
The heart block gets done.
